Rashi on Pesachim 59b:10:1.english: And shall we arise, etc. - It is a question.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:10:2.hebrew: שבקי' לקרא דהוא דחיק ומוקי אנפשיה - מדקשו קראי אהדדי, על כרחיך קראי גופייהו מוקמי אנפשייהו הכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:10:2.english: Leave the verse [alone], for it forces and establishes itself - Since the verses contradict one another, perforce the verses themselves establish themselves in this way.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:1.english: The Paschal offering that one slaughtered not for its own sake - For the sake of a peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:2.hebrew: או קיבל או הלך או זרק שלא לשמו - שבארבע עבודות הללו הפסח נפסל במחשבתן, אם לפסול אם לפגל, כדיליף בשמעתא קמייתא דזבחים (דף ד.):
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:2.english: Or received, or carried, or sprinkled not for its [own] purpose - For with these four services, the Paschal lamb is disqualified through [improper] intent during them, whether [an intent] to disqualify [it] or to render [it] piggul, as [the Gemara] derives in the first discussion of Zevachim (4a).

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:3.hebrew: או לשמו ושלא לשמו - בגמרא מפרש אי במחשבת עבודה אחת קאמר, אי במחשבת שתי עבודות, כגון קיבל לשמו וזרק שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:3.english: Or for its [own] purpose and not for its [own] purpose - In the Gemara it explains whether [the Mishnah] means with the intention of one service, [or] whether [it means] with the intention of two services, such as [where] he received [the blood] for its [own] purpose and sprinkled [it] not for its [own] purpose.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:4.hebrew: פסול - דכתיב זבח פסח הוא, שתהא זביחתו לשם פסח, וכתיב הוא, למעוטי נשחט שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:11:4.english: Disqualified - For it is written, "It is a Passover sacrifice" — [meaning] that its slaughter must be for the sake of a Passover [offering]; and it is written "it is" to exclude [an offering] slaughtered not for its own sake.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:13:1.hebrew: בעבודה אחת תנן - וחישב בה לשמו ושלא לשמו, ואפ"ה קתני פסול, ור' יוסי היא, דאמר במסכת תמורה (דף כה.) אף בגמר דבריו אדם נתפס דבוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:13:1.english: Did we learn [it] with regard to one rite - [meaning] that he had intent during it for its own purpose and not for its own purpose, and even so [the Mishnah] teaches [that it is] disqualified, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yosei, who said in Tractate Temurah (25a): even by the conclusion of his words a person is held bound.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:15:1.hebrew: דאי ר' מאיר האמר תפוס לשון ראשון - במסכת תמורה (ג"ז שם), גבי האומר הרי זו תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים: ר"מ אומר הרי זו תמורת עולה, ר' יוסי אומר דבריו קיימים, ותרעה עד שתומם ותמכר, ויביא בדמי חציה עולה ובדמי חציה שלמי':
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:15:1.english: For if [it accords with] Rabbi Meir, surely he said: Hold the first expression - In Tractate Temurah (this too is there), regarding one who says, "Behold, this is a substitute for a burnt-offering, a substitute for a peace-offering": Rabbi Meir says, "Behold, this is a substitute for a burnt-offering"; Rabbi Yosei says, "His words stand, and [the animal] shall graze until it becomes blemished and be sold, and he shall bring a burnt-offering with half of its proceeds and a peace-offering with half of its proceeds."

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:1:1.hebrew: והעלה הכהן את העולה ואת המנחה וגו' - בפר חטאת כתיב. ומדהוה ליה למיכתב "ואת העולה יעלה", וכתיב "והעלה", משמע: אפילו הביא העולה קודם לחטאת, יכפר:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:1:1.english: And the priest shall offer the burnt-offering and the meal-offering, etc. - It is written regarding the bull of the sin-offering. Since it should have written, "and the burnt-offering he shall offer," yet it is written, "and he shall offer [it, implying it was already offered]," [this] implies [that] even if he brought the burnt-offering before the sin-offering, it atones.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:2:1.hebrew: דסברי דיומא היא - כשמקטירים כל הלילה אברים שניתותרו מקרבנות שנשחטו ונזרק דמן קודם לתמיד, ויראו את האברים הללו, יהו סבורין שגם אלה ניתותרו וראויין להקטירם היום, ויקטירם ועברי אעשה דהשלמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:2:1.english: For they think that it is of that day - When they burn throughout the night limbs that were left over from offerings that were slaughtered and whose blood was sprinkled before the [afternoon] daily offering, and they see these limbs, they will think that these too were left over and are fit to be burned today, and they will burn them and transgress the positive commandment of completion.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:2:2.english: They are vigilant - And the one who brings them up there will inform his fellow priests, and they will be careful with them.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:3:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רב אשי כו' - אדרב פפא פריך, דאמר מלינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:3:1.english: Rav Ashi said to him, etc. - He raises an objection against Rav Pappa, who said [that] we leave [them] overnight.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:3:2.hebrew: מכדי כל כמה דלא מקטרי אמורין - דחטאת, כהנים בשר החטאת לא מצי אכלי, ובעלים לא הויא להו כפרה, ועדיין מחוסר כפורים הוא, והיאך יאכל בקדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:3:2.english: Now, as long as the sacrificial parts are not burned - of the sin-offering, the priests cannot eat the meat of the sin-offering, and the owners do not have atonement, and he is still lacking atonement, so how may he eat of the consecrated [food]?

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:3:3.english: With the breast and thigh - [Which are] given to the priests from the peace-offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:4:1.english: And they shall eat them - It is written regarding the consecration [of the priests].

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:4:2.english: With which atonement was made - [Scripture] wrote atonement alongside eating, to say that atonement also depends on eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:5:1.hebrew: כיון דלא אפשר - לאקטורינהו האידנא משום עשה דהשלמה, עשאום כמי שנטמאו או שאבדו, ומשתרו כהנים באכילת בשר, והויא כפרה לבעלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:5:1.english: Since it is impossible - to burn them now because of the positive commandment of completion, they rendered them as [sacrificial parts] that became ritually impure or were lost, and the priests are permitted to eat [the] meat, and there is atonement for the owners.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:6:1.hebrew: הא כל הלילה ילין - למטה, ומעלן ומקטירן כל הלילה, ואינו נפסל אלא אם כן מצאן בעלות השחר כשהוא למטה. אלמא כל הלילה ראוי להקטיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:6:1.english: But it may remain all night - Below [the altar], and one may bring them up and burn them all night, and it does not become disqualified unless [one] finds them at dawn while it is [still] below [the altar]. Thus, it is fit for burning all night.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:6:2.english: And it is written: Upon it complete - Which implies that nothing should be delayed after the daily afternoon offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:7:1.hebrew: כשנתותרו - מקרבנות שנזרק דמן קודם תמיד ולא הספיקו להקריב, דכיון דנראה להקרבה קודם לכן, על תמיד של שחר הוא מושלם:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:7:1.english: When they were left over - [That is, fats] from offerings whose blood was sprinkled before the [afternoon] daily offering and they did not have time to offer [them], for since it became fit for offering prior to that, it is [considered] completed upon the morning daily offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 59b:8:1.hebrew: הא כל הלילה ילין - ויקטירנו בלילי י"ט, ואע"פ שנותר מקרבן של חול, דהא י"ד שנזרק דם הפסח בו חול הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 59b:8:1.english: But it may remain all through the night - And one may burn it [on the altar] on the night of the Festival, even though it is left over from a weekday offering, for the fourteenth [of Nisan], on which the blood of the Paschal offering was sprinkled, is a weekday.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:15:1.hebrew: דאי ר' מאיר האמר תפוס לשון ראשון - אור"י, דרבא לטעמיה דאית ליה דפליגי בתפוס לשון ראשון, דאמרינן בפ"ב דזבחים (דף ל.): "עדיין היא מחלוקת", פירוש: אפילו בתמורת עולה ושלמים פליג ר"מ. ובלאו הכי הך דיוקא דהכא לא מיתוקם אלא אליבא דרבא, דמייתי לקמן בפירקין (פסחים דף סג.) גבי "אחרים אומרים הקדים מולים לערלים" כו', וסבר אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף, וכדרבא דאמר "עדיין היא מחלוקת", ופליגי בתפוס לשון ראשון אפילו בכי האי גוונא — אף על גב דאינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף וברגע אחרון יש לשניהם לחול, וסבר ר"מ התם תפוס לשון ראשון אע"פ שלא חל בשעה שאמר. דלרבה ואביי דלקמן, דסבירא להו דישנה לשחיטה מתחלה ועד סוף, חיילי תרווייהו אפילו לר"מ כמו שנאמר לקמן; וא"כ, לא יכשיר הכא לר"מ לשמו ושלא לשמו אפי' בעבודה אחת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:15:1.english: For if [it is according to] Rabbi Meir, surely he said: Hold [one accountable for] the first expression - Rabbi Yitzchak says that Rava [follows] his own reasoning, as he holds that they disagree regarding "hold [one accountable for] the first expression," as we say in the second chapter of Zevachim (30a): "It is still a dispute," meaning: even regarding a substitute [animal designated as] a burnt-offering and a peace-offering, Rabbi Meir disagrees. And even without this, this inference here can only be established according to Rava, who brings [this] later in our chapter (Pesachim 63a) regarding "Others say: If he placed the circumcised before the uncircumcised," etc., and he holds that slaughter takes effect only at the end, and [it is] in accordance with Rava, who said, "It is still a dispute," and they disagree regarding "hold [one accountable for] the first expression" even in such a case — even though slaughter takes effect only at the end and at the final moment both [intentions] can take effect, and Rabbi Meir holds there "hold [one accountable for] the first expression" even though it did not take effect at the time he spoke. For according to Rabbah and Abaye later, who hold that slaughter takes effect from beginning to end, both [intentions] take effect even according to Rabbi Meir, as will be stated later; and if so, here he would not deem valid, according to Rabbi Meir, [an offering slaughtered] for its own sake and not for its own sake even during a single service.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:5:1.hebrew: עשאום כמי שנטמאו אימורין או אבדו - למאן דאמר (לקמן פסחים דף עז:) אין הציץ מרצה על העולין, ניחא הא דנקט הכא "שנטמאו או אבדו"; אבל ברייתא דלקמן (פסחים דף פ:): "על מה הציץ מרצה? על הדם ועל החלב" — צ"ל הואיל ומדרבנן לא מרצה, הוי כאילו אבדו האימורין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:5:1.english: They rendered them as [a case where] the sacrificial parts became ritually impure or were lost - According to the one who says (later, Pesachim 77b) [that] the tzitz [High Priest's frontplate] does not effect acceptance for the portions that go up [on the altar], that which [the Gemara] mentions here, "that became ritually impure or were lost," is understandable; however, [according to] the baraita later (Pesachim 80b): "For what does the tzitz effect acceptance? For the blood and for the fat," one must say [that] since rabbinically it does not effect acceptance, it is as if the sacrificial parts were lost.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:5:2.hebrew: יכול נטמאו או שאבדו לא יהו הכהנים כו' - הכי סלקא מסקנא הכא, דאי לא אכלי כהנים, לא מכפרי בעלים ולא משתרו לאכול בקדשים. ומקשה ריב"א, דבהאשה רבה (יבמות דף צ.) אמר: "ת"ש, דם שנטמא וזרקו — בשוגג הורצה, במזיד לא הורצה. והא הכא דמדאורייתא ארצויי מרצי כו'". ומשני: "מאי לא הורצה? להתיר בשר באכילה, אבל בעלים מתכפרין". אלמא, אף על גב דבשר אינו נאכל — בעלים מתכפרין! וי"ל, דהיכא דחזי לאכילה מדאורייתא, מתכפרין; והכא בעי למימר דכל כמה דלא חזו כהנים לאכילת בשר, לא מתכפרים בעלים. ומיהו קשה: מנטמא בשר, היאך זורק את הדם? הא אין לבשר שעת היתר לכהנים! ונראה לפרש, דכל זמן דחזי בשר לאכילה, לא מתכפרי בעלים עד שיאכלו כהנים; אבל אם נטמא אחרי כן, או יצא, או נעשה נותר — מתכפרי בעלים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:5:2.english: "I might [have thought] that if [the sacrificial parts] became ritually impure or were lost, the priests would not [be entitled]," etc. - This is how the conclusion here turns out: that if the priests do not eat [the meat], the owners do not achieve atonement and are not permitted to eat sacrificial meat. And Riva raises a difficulty, for in [the chapter] HaIshah Rabbah (Yevamot 90a) [the Gemara] says: "Come [and] hear: Blood that became ritually impure and one sprinkled it — [if he did so] unwittingly, it is accepted; [if] intentionally, it is not accepted. Now here, by Torah law it is indeed accepted, etc." And [the Gemara] answers: "What does 'it is not accepted' mean? [It is not accepted] to permit the meat for eating, but the owners achieve atonement." Thus [we see that] even though the meat is not eaten, the owners achieve atonement! And one can answer that wherever [the meat] is fit for eating by Torah law, [the owners] achieve atonement; whereas here [the Gemara] means to say that as long as the priests are not fit to eat the meat, the owners do not achieve atonement. However, there is a difficulty: [what about] when the meat became ritually impure — how can one sprinkle the blood? Surely the meat has no moment of permissibility for the priests! And it appears [proper] to explain that as long as the meat is fit for eating, the owners do not achieve atonement until the priests eat [it]; however, if it became ritually impure afterward, or went out [of the Temple courtyard], or became notar [leftover beyond its time], the owners achieve atonement.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:8:1.hebrew: ולא עולת חול ביו"ט - הקשה ריב"א: דהא קרא בשבת כתיב דחמיר, אבל ביו"ט דקיל, מנא לן דלא קרבה? וי"ל דאתיא כרבי עקיבא, דאמר בסוף אלו קשרים (שבת דף קיד.): "עולת שבת" — לימד על חלבי שבת שקרבין בי"ט. ומשמע ליה קרא: "עולת שבת זו בשבת אחרת", דהיינו של שבת בי"ט, מכלל דשל חול בי"ט לא קרבה. וקשה: לר' עקיבא, תיפוק לי' דחלבי שבת קריבין בי"ט מקרא דהכא, ד"לא ילין" — הא כל הלילה ילין, דלכל הפחות מיתוקם בארבעה עשר שחל להיות בשבת? תימה לר"י: הא קרא בנותר דבשר מיירי, דהא לקמן (פסחים דף סג:) מחייב שוחט על חמץ אחד מבני חבורה מדכתיב "לא ילין" בתריה, דמשמע הני דקיימינן עלי' ב"לא ילין". ו"כל הלילה ילין" — כדר' עקיבא אוקימנא לסוגיא דהכא, ושמעינן ליה לר' עקיבא דפסח נאכל כל הלילה עד שעת חפזון. ואיכא למימר דמשמע ליה למסדר הש"ס דקרא בכל הזבח מיירי, בין בבשר ובין באימורין; ומדלא כתיב "חלב" כמו גבי "חלב חגי", ומדלא כתיב גבי אכילה ד"ואכלו את הבשר" כדכתב התם "לא תותירו", ש"מ דבתרווייהו משתעי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:8:1.english: And the burnt-offering of a weekday is not [offered] on a Festival - Riva (R. Yitzchak ben Asher) raised a difficulty: This verse is written regarding Shabbat, which is stringent, but regarding a Festival, which is lenient, from where do we [know] that it is not offered? And one can say that [this] follows R. Akiva, who said at the end of [the chapter] Elu Kesharim (Shabbat 114a): "The burnt-offering of Shabbat" teaches regarding the fats of Shabbat that they are offered on a Festival. And the verse implies to him: "the burnt-offering of this Shabbat [may be offered] on another Shabbat," that is, [the fats] of Shabbat on a Festival — from which it follows by implication that [those] of a weekday are not offered on a Festival. And it is difficult: According to R. Akiva, let him derive that the fats of Shabbat are offered on a Festival from the verse here, for [it states] "it shall not remain overnight [until morning]" — implying that all night it may remain, which at the very least is established [as referring] to the fourteenth [of Nisan] that falls on Shabbat! It is astonishing to the Ri (R. Yitzchak): This verse speaks of leftover meat, for later (Pesachim 63b) [the Gemara] holds liable one who slaughters [the Paschal offering] over leaven [belonging to] one of the members of the group, because it is written "it shall not remain overnight" right after it, which implies [that] those [whom] we were discussing are subject to "it shall not remain overnight." And [as for] "all night it may remain" — we have established our sugya here according to R. Akiva, and we have heard regarding R. Akiva that the Paschal offering may be eaten all night until the time of haste [i.e., morning]. And one can say that it seemed to the redactor of the Talmud that the verse speaks of the entire sacrifice, both the meat and the sacrificial parts; and since it does not write "fat" as [it does] regarding "the fat of My festival offering" [Exodus 23:18], and since it does not write [it] regarding eating — [namely], "and they shall eat the meat" — as it writes there, "you shall not leave over" [Exodus 12:10], we learn from this that it speaks of both of them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:9:1.hebrew: בארבעה עשר שחל להיות בשבת עסקינן - בירושלמי דייק מקרא דלא ילין חלב חגי כה"ג, ומוקי לה נמי ר' אבהו בי"ד שחל להיות בשבת. ופריך: דלא מצי לאוקמי בשבת, דחגי כתיב, דהיינו חגיגה הבאה עם הפסח, דלא דחיא שבת, כדאמר לקמן באלו דברים (פסחים דף סט:). ומפרש דה"ק: שמרהו שלא יבא לידי בל ילין, שיקריבהו מבעוד יום בשעה הראויה לו. ותימה על ירושלמי דפריך מינה, דהאי קרא דחלב חגי דבחגיגת חמשה עשר מיירי כדמוכח באלו דברים. הקשה רשב"א לבן תימא, דדריש לקמן באלו דברים (פסחים דף ע.) חגיגה הבאה עם הפסח הרי היא כפסח, דזבח חג — זה חגיגה: היכי מיתוק' האי קרא בשבת? הא מודה דלא דחיא שבת, כדמוכח התם! וי"ל: דבן תימא יסבור כר' ישמעאל, דאמר באלו קשרים (שבת דף קיד:) דחלבי חול קריבין בי"ט. אי נמי, בן תימא יפרש: שמרהו שלא יבא לידי בל ילין, כדמפרש בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 59b:9:1.english: "We are dealing with [a case where] the fourteenth [of Nisan] occurs on Shabbat" - In the Yerushalmi, [the Gemara] infers similarly from the verse "the fat of My festival offering shall not remain overnight," and R' Abbahu likewise establishes it [as referring to] the fourteenth [of Nisan] that occurs on Shabbat. And [the Yerushalmi] objects that one cannot establish it on Shabbat, for "My festival offering" [chaggi] is written, which is the chagigah offering that comes with the Pesach offering, which does not override Shabbat, as is stated later in [the chapter] Eilu Devarim (Pesachim 69b). And [the Yerushalmi] explains that this is what it means: guard it so that it does not come to [transgressing] "it shall not remain overnight," [meaning] that one should offer it while it is still day, at its proper time. And it is astonishing regarding the Yerushalmi that it objects from it, for this verse of "the fat of My festival offering" deals with the chagigah of the fifteenth [of Nisan], as is proven in Eilu Devarim. Rashba asked regarding Ben Teima, who expounds later in Eilu Devarim (Pesachim 70a) [that] the chagigah that comes with the Pesach is like the Pesach, for "the festival sacrifice" [zevach chag] — this is the chagigah: how can this verse be established on Shabbat? Behold, he agrees that it does not override Shabbat, as is proven there! And one can answer that Ben Teima holds like R' Yishmael, who says in [the chapter] Eilu Kesharim (Shabbat 114b) that the fats of a weekday [offering] may be offered on Yom Tov. Alternatively, Ben Teima explains [the verse as]: guard it so that it does not come to [transgressing] "it shall not remain overnight," as is explained in the Yerushalmi.
